result.Method of Attack: Remote code execution via unauthenticated PUT request followed by GET request triggering deserialization; Exploitation of path traversal and deserialization flaws; Uploading malicious files using legitimate-looking PUT requests; Bypassing traditional security tools using base64-encoded payloads
result.Impacted Systems: Enterprise and government systems running vulnerable Apache Tomcat versions
result.Attack Vector: Writable directory access with vulnerable configurations such as file-based session storage; Default session persistence mechanism and partial PUT support exploitation; Internet-wide scanning and exploitation targeting vulnerable Tomcat servers
result.Indicators of Compromise: Legitimate-looking PUT requests carrying base64-encoded payloads; Proof-of-concept exploit published on GitHub; Automated scanning activity from multiple countries; Payloads attempting to establish remote shells or deploy web-based backdoors
